target.title: fix(duckduckgo): forward abort signal when web search runs are canceled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DuckDuckGo web searches continue running after the agent run is canceled. The web search runtime already threads the caller's `AbortSignal` into `execute(args, { signal })`, but the DuckDuckGo provider discarded it — so aborted runs still consumed network resources and delayed timeout fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider now forwards `context?.signal` to the client, and the client passes it to `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` (which already supports `signal?: AbortSignal` in the shared SDK). The pattern matches the searxng fix in #104216 — one provider per PR, no SDK or core changes needed.

## User Impact

- Canceled agent runs stop in-flight DuckDuckGo web searches promptly instead of draining them to completion.
- Aborted searches no longer delay fallback to the next configured provider.

## Evidence

### Regression test — signal flows from execute context to the client

The new test creates an `AbortController`, calls `tool.execute({ query: "openclaw docs" }, { signal: controller.signal })`, and asserts `runDuckDuckGoSearch` was called with that exact `controller.signal`. DuckDuckGo has no category fallback or provider-loop complexity — the signal passes straight through to `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint`, which already accepts `signal?: AbortSignal` in the SDK.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/duckduckgo/
 ✓ 12/12 passed (including new signal forwarding test)
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.ts extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-client.ts extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.test.ts
✓ clean
```

### tsgo

```
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs | grep -i duckduckgo
(no errors — DuckDuckGo module typechecks clean)
```

### Signal path verification

The full signal path is: `src/web-search/runtime.ts:489` → `tool.execute(args, { signal })` → `context?.signal` → `runDuckDuckGoSearch({ signal })` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint({ signal })`. Each link is a pass-through parameter — DuckDuckGo adds no transformation, fallback, or retry logic. The SDK's `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` handles `AbortSignal` natively as a fetch option.
